A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work, with matching authors, title, core method, and retained experiments. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–D are readable and support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v3 reports original autoencoder training, memorization/generalization analyses, data-free reconstruction experiments, and OOD detection results in Sections 3–4 and Appendix B.

after.justification: v4 retains those original results and adds OOD baseline comparisons, convergence diagnostics, self-supervised and language-model studies, and decoded-attractor visualizations.

M1.justification: The autoencoder iteration and trajectory-based OOD score remain unchanged. Appendix B.8 adds procedural adaptations: pairing frozen DINOv2/SigLIP2 encoders with pretrained decoders and iterating language-model residual-stream representations. These extend the construction of the self-map while retaining the underlying iteration.

E1.justification: v3 evaluates image data and synthetic noise. Appendix B.8.2 of v4 introduces text-domain latent-dynamics evaluation using Pile samples with Qwen3 and SmolLM2, substantially extending domain coverage. This evaluates representation dynamics, not next-token prediction accuracy. Existing vision datasets are retained.

E2.justification: v4 Appendix B.3/Table 1 extends the existing KNN-only OOD comparison with Mahalanobis feature distance and reconstruction error on the same four OOD datasets. The orthogonal-basis comparator in the reconstruction experiments remains unchanged.

E3.justification: New diagnostics use 300 iterations on 500 ImageNet training images for DINOv2/SigLIP2 and 1,000 Pile samples for the language models, measuring residual and embedding norms. A ViT-MAE diagnostic uses 2,000 ImageNet samples. These are added evaluation designs; the retained reconstruction and OOD protocols are unchanged.

E4.justification: v4 substantially extends diagnostic analyses: Appendix B.4.1 directly examines pretrained ViT-MAE convergence, B.8 tests whether iterative dynamics remain bounded beyond conventional autoencoders, and B.9 examines the visual content of Stable Diffusion attractors. The earlier initialization, rank, overfitting, and convergence-speed analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions report mean and standard deviation over attractors and retain the 10-seed initialization study. v4 specifies no changed run counts, confidence-interval definitions, or significance-testing procedures. Shaded bands in the added plots do not introduce a documented new uncertainty-estimation practice.

E6.justification: The original Figure 5 scores are retained, but v4 adds substantial results. Table 1 reports SUN397 FPR/AUROC of 82.00/58.00 for Mahalanobis and 91.80/49.50 for reconstruction, versus 29.60/91.20 for attractor trajectories. Figures 12 and 16–18 add convergence curves, bounded but nonzero residual plateaus beyond AEs, and texture-like decoded attractors.

T1.justification: Appendix C adds a chain-rule and spectral-norm derivation connecting weight decay to contraction under 1-Lipschitz activation assumptions. Section 2.1 adds C < 1 to its Banach statement and fixes the Jacobian-norm expression; Theorem 1 qualifies score proportionality as local. The substantive Appendix A proofs remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction’s contribution list, and main conclusion retain the same claims about AE latent vector fields, memorization/generalization, data-free weight probing, and distribution-shift detection. The new non-AE studies are explicitly presented as preliminary extensions rather than revised central contributions.

C2.justification: Section 6.1 and Appendix B.8 revisit applicability beyond AEs, discuss residual plateaus as possible attractor regions or near-unit contraction, and identify unresolved attractor and positional-embedding questions. B.9 clarifies that decoded Stable Diffusion attractors exhibit geometric and texture patterns. Section 4.1 also removes the asserted equivalence between orthogonal-basis OMP and PCA.

D1.justification: Appendix B.8 identifies the pretrained decoder source, Qwen3-0.6B and SmolLM2-1.7B variants, and the representation interfaces used for iteration. These provide technical information for the added studies. Existing architecture tables, training hyperparameters, stopping criteria, hardware, and software disclosures remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v4 adds attribution to Sun et al. for the retained KNN baseline and references supporting the new models, Pile data, pretrained decoders, positional embeddings, and latent reasoning discussion. Section 5’s related-work account and the central positioning relative to prior autoencoder research remain substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: Most existing prose and section ordering are preserved. v4 clarifies FPR95 earlier, expands and separates limitations into Section 6.1, adds appendix subsections and acknowledgments, and updates the affiliation and conference header. This is localized editing and structural extension rather than extensive rewriting.

P2.justification: v4 substantially expands the visual evidence with an extended OOD table and separate figures for ViT-MAE convergence, self-supervised dynamics, language-model dynamics, and decoded attractors. Figure 5 gains explicit histogram panel labels and a clearer caption. Existing plots and architecture tables are preserved with renumbering and layout reflow.

improvement.justification: Table 1 broadens v3’s KNN-only OOD validation, while the convergence diagnostics and decoded-attractor examples improve empirical support and interpretability. The gains are limited: nonzero residual plateaus in Figures 16–17 do not establish convergence to point attractors, despite their contraction interpretation, and the central Appendix A proofs remain unchanged.
